Same stock, two exchanges, two prices. I track 52 stock, index, FX and commodity perps on Hyperliquid and Lighter to see if those gaps can actually be traded after fees and spreads.

Overnight (18:00–06:00 UTC): one trade cleared the bar, in UNITREE.

UNITREE: Hyperliquid's Paragon listing traded 0.42% above XYZ's for 1h+ during Asian hours, peaking at 1.24%.

Short Paragon at $111.40, long XYZ at $110.93. The gap closed and overshot by 0.17% within 1.3h.

On $10k a side: +$59 gross, −$30 fees and spread (est.), +$29 net.

Hyperliquid's Paragon market is the rich venue: its listings sat a median 0.26% above the same assets elsewhere. But its books cost 0.18% to get in and out of $10k, vs 0.02% on XYZ, which eats most of it.

Funding: UNITREE paid -222% a year on Lighter vs -369% on Paragon. Shorts pay on both venues: a crowded short. The carry is worth ≈$40/day per $10k, but the price gap between those two swung 1.55% (≈$155) in the same 12h.

Scorecard, last 3 days: 10 trades, 7 profitable, +$126 net on $10k a side.

The rule: at least 0.10% left after crossing both order books, held for an hour, real volume on both sides, closed the same day. Market orders, fees included.

Simulated, not advice.
